svg.title: P012 · Price and discount statistics per category
svg.desc: One row of price statistics per category. The extended example puts product IDs 1, 2, 3 in category 10 and IDs 4, 5 in category 20. Category 10 has prices 80, 100, 30. Its minimum is 30, maximum is 100 and average is 210 / 3 = 70. Read the products again. ID 2 contributes one full-price flag. IDs 3 and 5 have unusable market prices and contribute NULL percentages. Category 10 averages (20% + 0%) / 2 = 10%. Category 20 averages its single known percentage, 25%. All five products still count.
svg.text: Price and discount statistics per category
One row of price statistics per category.
In category 10, should a zero market price remove the product from its sale-price average?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.
The extended example puts product IDs 1, 2, 3 in category 10 and IDs 4, 5 in category 20.
Which prices feed the three price metrics?
Category 10 has prices 80, 100, 30. Its minimum is 30, maximum is 100 and average is 210 / 3 = 70.
What can each product contribute to the discount?
